Data quality checks for the item-revision loop

Source: R/loop.R
loop_checker.Rd

loop_checker() makes the checker step of revision_loop(). It runs synthetic_pretest() on the round's responses (all respondent models pooled) and screens the respondents for answer patterns that make the data unusable.

Usage

loop_checker(
  thresholds = list(),
  irt = FALSE,
  n_pa = 20,
  straightline_sd = 0.5,
  inconsistency = 0.5,
  max_careless = 0.05
)

Arguments

thresholds

thresholds for the item flags, as in synthetic_pretest().

irt

also fit graded response models in synthetic_pretest() for its slope flags? Off by default, because loop_irt() fits them as the evaluator.

n_pa

number of random data sets for parallel analysis.

straightline_sd, inconsistency, max_careless

the respondent screening rules (see above).

Value

A function for the checker argument of revision_loop().

Details

Item flags (from synthetic_pretest(), with its thresholds): low_variance, key, weak and other_scale with severity "fail", and redundant with severity "warn".

Respondent screening. A respondent is unusable when the SD of their answers is below straightline_sd (straight-lining), when the mean keyed difference between their positive and reverse-keyed items is above inconsistency times the width of the scale (they ignore the keys), or when more than half of their answers are missing. The share of unusable respondents is the stat careless_share, flagged (with item and scale NA) when it is above max_careless. These are absolute rules, because the respondents are compared with no real people here.

Stats: alpha, mean_r and n_factors per scale; own_scale, reverse_ok, n_factors_all, scales and careless_share over all items; and per item mean, sd, item_rest, max_r and (with irt = TRUE) slope.

See also

revision_loop(), synthetic_pretest()

Examples

ins <- sc_instrument(hexaco_items[hexaco_items$trait == "H", ], scale = c(1, 7))
syn <- generate_synthetic(ins, sc_model("mock"), respondents = 30, cache = FALSE)
chk <- loop_checker(n_pa = 5)
out <- chk(syn, ins$items, list(construct = loop_construct("H", scale = c(1, 7))))
head(out$flags)
